claims.text: A hybrid approach coupling metadynamics with a machine-learned interatomic potential can reproduce solid and liquid free energies near fusion conditions.
The hybrid approach can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
Training the machine-learned potential on a limited ab initio molecular-dynamics dataset is sufficient for the proposed free-energy calculations.
The hybrid approach would cost substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
Full ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations should be replaced by constrained metadynamics driven by a calibrated machine-learned potential.
Calibration against high-fidelity ab initio data ensures retention of vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration effects.
Initial tests will cover well-characterized elemental and binary systems near their fusion temperatures.
The machine-learning model captures effective potential-energy landscapes containing local structural fluctuations and dynamic disorder.
Strategically selected ab initio training data and metadynamics enable efficient exploration of phase space.
Efficient phase-space exploration permits approximation of full free-energy evaluations without extensive molecular dynamics.
The proposed mechanism reduces computational cost while preserving the essential entropy contributions.

For elemental and binary systems, fusion and high-temperature free energies, latent heats, and transition temperatures will deviate by less than 5% from explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD results.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by at least five- to ten-fold for elemental and binary systems.
Latent heat and melting temperature can be derived as observables from the calculated phase free energies.
The expected applicability boundary is elemental and binary alloys near their melting points.
Extension to multicomponent high-entropy systems requires additional validation because of their increased configurational complexity.
Conventional explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD calculate free energies with full vibrational and electronic coupling at high computational cost.
Vibrational-density-of-states spectra can verify retention of anharmonic and electron–vibration features.
Deviation exceeding 5% in phase free energies or derived observables relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD would falsify the hypothesis.
